svg.title: SeLo graph prompt pipeline
svg.desc: Complete editable SVG reconstruction of the original figure. Base frames: left input image patches and graph nodes, central top vision-graph/prompted-feature/GNN pipeline, legend, and three lower prompt examples. Conduction inventories include: image patch grid linked to graph nodes through an encoder; top block with vision graph structure, semantic low-rank decomposition, prompted graph features, GNN block, downstream head and loss; legend with add/product/frozen/trainable symbols and prompt color matrices; bottom SeLo-Graph Prompt, SeLo-Edge Prompt, and SeLo-Node Prompt panels with graph structures, dashed virtual nodes, equation labels, feature bars, MLPs, prompt matrices, operators, trainable flames and arrows. SAM mappings are used only for confirmed small icon/picture crops, preserving the original crop coordinates.

g.desc: Origin is the upper image patch grid; downward conduction reaches the blue double arrow and graph nodes, then rightward to encoder.
Origin is the Vision Graph Structure title and dashed structure frame. The graph flows rightward through decomposition prompts to prompted graph features, then GNN layers and downstream head.
Origin is upper-left add/product symbols; rightward conduction defines feature color swatches and prompt matrices. Symmetry basis: two-column legend with icon column and feature-matrix column.

Origin is graph panel title and graph at upper left. Downward/rightward conduction reaches virtual nodes and the blue graph-prompt module. Central graph symmetry is a connected network with dashed virtual-node augmentation.

Origin is upper edge subgraph. Downward conduction reaches the cream SeLo-Edge prompt panel. Symmetry basis: source feature Xn flows through MLP and prompt/product/add operations to context feature Xc.

Origin is title and upper graph. Downward conduction reaches green node-prompt panel. Symmetry basis: node feature Xi transforms through MLP to semantic feature and product with node prompt matrix, then added with residual path.
